description:
Hi everyone!

I’m Ángel Villón, a Software Engineering student (backend, APIs, DevOps).

For this NASA challenge, I’m building an astronaut health monitoring platform to track real-time telemetry and detect physiological anomalies.

Looking for: Someone in Medicine, Nursing, Biomedical Engineering, or Life Sciences to lead the clinical logic (vital thresholds, triage protocols, and research validation).

I’ll cover the backend and deployment. Let’s team up!
summary:
ASTHA (Autonomous Space Telemetry & Health Analytics) is a 100% offline clinical PWA for missions to the Moon and Mars. Built with Svelte 5, TypeScript, Web Workers, uPlot, and on-demand Three.js, it operates without internet (Zero-WAN) and integrates a deterministic engine based on NASA-STD-3001 and the NASA R.I.D.G.E. framework.

It addresses the challenge of diagnosing and treating medical emergencies when radio delay with Earth reaches 22 minutes each way (44 minutes round-trip) and evacuation is impossible. ASTHA classifies vital signs and habitat parameters (ppCO₂, radiation, pressure, O₂), detects early drifts using Modified Z-Score (MAD) and 7-day regression, and executes 10 cross-correlation rules (SANS, hypercapnia, solar particle events [SPE], and renal lithiasis). It presents each finding on an interactive anatomical model (3D/SVG) with step-by-step countermeasures (≤ 4 steps), encrypted tamper-evident storage (AES-GCM/Ed25519), CRDT synchronization, and cryptographically signed exports for Earth.

Its significance lies in transforming complex telemetry into autonomous, actionable clinical decisions in situ for non-medical crews beyond Earth orbit.
details:
What does it do and how does it work?

ASTHA (Autonomous Space Telemetry & Health Analytics) is a clinical PWA designed to operate 100% offline (Zero-WAN) during long-duration space missions. Its architecture separates the user interface from critical logic using two dedicated Web Workers:

  1. Clinical Engine (clinical.worker): A pure, deterministic core with no network or DOM access that receives a compact data window and evaluates in milliseconds:
    1. Tri-state classification (Nominal, Caution, Critical): Evaluates 10 physiological parameters and 6 habitat environmental parameters (ppCO₂, cabin pressure, O₂, radiation, temperature, and humidity) in compliance with NASA-STD-3001, applying the most severe band rule when gaps occur.
    2. Sustained conditions and early drift: Requires ≥ 2 consecutive days to confirm criticality in HRV (< 20 ms) and sleep (< 5.5 h), calculates the Modified Z-Score with MAD against each astronaut's personal baseline (days 1–14, threshold |Mᵢ| ≥ 2.5), and runs a 7-day rolling linear regression (O(1)) to project threshold crossings before severe symptoms appear.
    3. Cross-correlation and cumulative dose: Applies 10 multi-variable clinical rules (hypercapnia, early SANS, solar particle events [SPE], hypercalciuria-induced renal calculi, and orthostatic intolerance) alongside cumulative radiation dose tracking.
    4. Anatomical triage and countermeasures: Maps findings across 7 organ systems and 5 body regions on an interactive anatomical model (on-demand Three.js 3D + SVG fallback), displays historical trends with reference bands and baselines (uPlot), and deploys actionable protocols in ≤ 4 steps with automatic alternatives if onboard equipment is out of service, plus a gamification module (XP, levels, and streaks) that never interferes with alerts.
    5. Offline simulator and scientific reference: Includes a 180-day mission clock for 4 crew members, 6 crisis scenarios (A–F: SPE, acute SANS, CO₂ micro-leak, hypercalciuria/renal stone, sleep/HRV deprivation, and compound failure), loading of a 90-day reference dataset calibrated with OSD-574, and an offline explorer of 116 NASA OSDR human studies.
  2. Data, Cryptography, and Resilience Layer (dataSync.worker): Persists telemetry in IndexedDB inside AES-GCM-256 encrypted envelopes, signs every operation and export for Mission Control (DSN) in compressed JSON format (gzip) using Ed25519, validates integrity against radiation-induced bit flips (SEU) with SHA-256 and automatic quarantine, maintains a hash-chained audit log, and replicates changes via CRDTs with Hybrid Logical Clocks (HLC). It also includes a WebSocket client (SyncClient) and an OpenAPI 3.1.0 specification ready to couple with a future local Sync Hub on a closed network (astha.local).

What are its benefits?

• True medical autonomy without Earth: Eliminates live-link dependency when communication latency reaches up to 22 minutes each way (44 minutes round-trip).

• Proactive detection and fewer false alarms: Combines individual baselines (MAD), 7-day trends, and cross-correlation across environment + vital signs + symptoms reported in just a few taps.

• Immediate action by non-medical personnel: Translates complex alerts into plain-language instructions of at most 4 steps using only real onboard resources (LBNP, ARED, CDRA/LiOH, Med Kits Alpha/Bravo, solar storm shelter).

• Onboard privacy and security: Implements serverless cryptographic access control (each crew member decrypts their own record with their PIN, and only the Crew Medical Officer can decrypt the entire crew's records), while the lock screen hides sensitive medical data yet still allows critical cabin-wide alerts (Code Red SPE) to broadcast.

• Low power consumption and extreme lightness: Zero runtime CDNs, cache-only Service Worker, pure OLED black background (#030712), 630 nm spectral night mode, critical battery mode dropping to 0.2 fps when charge falls to ≤ 15%, and a final production bundle under 1 MB (within a 5 MB configured budget).

What is the expected impact of the project?

To reduce the critical time between detecting physiological deterioration or an environmental failure and executing the right countermeasure during Artemis missions and Mars transits where medical evacuation is impossible (No MEDEVAC). By doing so, it aims to prevent irreversible harm—such as vision loss from SANS, hypoxia/hypercapnia from CO₂ pockets, acute radiation syndrome from SPEs, or renal lithiasis driven by microgravity bone loss (1.0–1.5% per month)—while encouraging daily preventive habits and delivering auditable, cryptographically signed clinical packages to the Flight Surgeon on Earth.

Tools, languages, hardware, and software used

• Languages & Frontend: TypeScript, Svelte 5 (reactive runes), CSS with custom design tokens (native system fonts, zero external dependencies), and Vite 8.

• Visualization & Audio: uPlot (high-performance 2D Canvas charts), Three.js (on-demand 3D rendering at 0 FPS when idle) + native interactive SVG, and locally synthesized Web Audio API with zero external media files.

• Concurrency, Storage & Cryptography: Web Workers, Service Worker, IndexedDB, WebCrypto API (AES-GCM, PBKDF2, Ed25519, SHA-256), and CompressionStream (gzip).

• Quality, Containers & Deployment: Vitest (fake-indexeddb), svelte-check, ESLint, multi-stage Docker (node:22-alpine + nginxinc/nginx-unprivileged:1.27-alpine in read_only mode), Docker Compose, Caddy 2.9 (automatic TLS), and GitHub Actions (CI/CD to GHCR and deployment on Linux / AWS Lightsail or EC2).

• Target Hardware Considered in Design: Flight tablets and bulkhead touch consoles with OLED displays, potential gloved operation, and future telemetry peripherals (such as Astroskin/Bio-Monitor, CANS dosimeters, and the ECLSS bus via the POST /ingest/telemetry contract).

How is the project creative?

• Near-zero energy 3D rendering: The Three.js 3D anatomical viewer wakes up only upon user interaction or state change and drops back to 0 FPS when idle, with instant SVG fallback if the WebGL context fails or power survival mode is triggered.

• Serverless CRDT + Zero-Knowledge Cryptography: Synchronization and gamification are built on convergent structures (LWW-Map, G-Set, PN-Counter) over per-crew encrypted envelopes; even nodes without permission to read another crew member's clinical data can store and relay their envelopes and verify Ed25519 signatures.

• In-browser self-protection against space radiation (SEU): The client verifies the signature and SHA-256 integrity of its local IndexedDB envelopes, isolates corrupted blocks in quarantine, and can restore them from local replicas.

• Privacy-preserving emergency escalation: An unacknowledged critical alert progressively escalates to the CMO (2 min) and cabin-wide (5 min), overlaying even the lock screen without exposing personal diagnoses in plaintext.

What factors did the team consider?

  1. NASA R.I.D.G.E. and NASA-STD-3001 biomedical risks: Strict calibration of spaceflight physiological and environmental ranges rather than generic terrestrial values.
  2. Ergonomics in microgravity and gloved operation: Minimum 48 × 48 px touch targets and ≥ 12 px spacing to prevent accidental taps while floating.
  3. Visual accessibility and neuro-ocular fatigue (WCAG 2.1 AAA): Minimum ≥ 7:1 contrast across all dark surfaces, prohibition of pure red as text color, double/triple encoding (color + icon/symbol + hatched pattern + pulse) for color blindness, tabular numerals, and a 630 nm night filter to preserve dark adaptation in the cabin.
  4. Thermal and electrical constraints without natural convection: Complete elimination of active polling, bundle compression under 1 MB, Survival mode, and controlled degradation under critical battery levels.
  5. Content security and network isolation: Strict CSP policy, explicit blocking of external origins in the Service Worker, and transparent distinction between synthetic demo data and NASA OSDR reference studies/series.

AI USE:

AI was used exclusively during development as a coding assistant (Svelte 5, TypeScript, unit tests) and for rapid technical decision-making (evaluating architecture trade-offs and structuring NASA-STD-3001 clinical rules). The runtime clinical engine is 100% deterministic with zero AI dependencies.
